summary: Aermotor LS-40 lookout in the Flatrock State Wildlife Area; land 1942, erected 1943; height and county disputed by sources; NHLR-registered August 2026.

access.note: The Register places it in the Flatrock State Wildlife Area but gives no visiting rules

visit.trail_note: The Register says it is climbable only to the top, just beneath the cab; there is no functioning catwalk and only a locked hatch into the cab. Cab condition is unknown. No visiting rules are stated.

Annual report for FY1969-70: a deep well was drilled, a pump installed, and a pump house, water line and pressure tank added at the towersite
The residence at the towersite was remodeled and a room added; the residence, not the tower
Register: decent condition, light graffiti, some wobbly wood planks, cab condition unknown

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register places the tower in Texas County (Flatrock State Wildlife Area). The Central Lookouts list and page place it in Shannon County (Angeline Conservation Area). The story reports both and does not choose.

The Register gives 100 feet (Aermotor LS-40). The 1943 annual report quoted by Central Lookouts gives 50 feet. The sources do not say whether the 1943 figure describes the tower standing today. The story reports both, and no height is set in facts.

sources.title: Shooting the Smoke
sources.publisher: Missouri Conservationist, Missouri Department of Conservation

notes_for_editor: Two conflicts are left open. Height: the Register says 100 ft; the 1943 annual report quoted on Central Lookouts says 50 ft. The brief's height_m 15.2 is the 50-ft figure, so it is left out of facts for the editor to decide. County: the brief and the Register say Texas County; the Central Lookouts list and page say Shannon County. The Central page's annual-report entries describe a 1943 steel tower, then later steel towers replacing temporary wooden ones in 1957-58 and 1962; the story reports this without choosing. The Register's land and erection dates are attributed to online resources, and the story says so. The brief's agency name follows the Register; the Central site uses 'Missouri Conservation Commission' for the same agency's earlier name. No staffing or fire data was found in any source read. Visiting rules are not stated. A Facebook group snippet mentioning the Angeline Conservation Area was not used. No photos added.
